title: Can an AI build a 30-second dance animation all by itself from just three sentences?
summary: Verdict: yes. Zero human hands touched it, and three short instructions produced a finished 30.000-second dance animation (720×960 @24fps, H.264+AAC, just 5.0 MB).
stats: Just 3 instructions to the assistant (Hermes): ① build a Hatsune Miku model in Blender → ② continue → ③ once acceptance passes, make a 30-second dance video; no reference images, no storyboard, the AI designed everything itself

Yes, and not one human touch the whole way: modeling → fixing → rigging → choreography → music → rendering were all done by the AI alone. Model acceptance passed 6/6 rounds, the final cut is exactly 30.000 seconds, and it fixed all 3 render crashes by itself

On a Mac mini M2 16GB (macOS 26.6.2), the AI drove Blender 5.2 headless in the background, using render-image checks (vision_analyze) as its eyes: 19 self-checks, each round finding flaws and fixing them
227 messages · 108 tool calls; input tokens ▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮ 530K vs output ▮▮ 109K (thinking took 63K), so most of the burn is on the input side
findings: The model ran 6 rounds of 'render → look at the image → fix': one defect class per round (headphone band, bangs, tie, skirt/boots), and the final acceptance passed all 6 rounds (6/6 PASS)
Memory blew up halfway (OOM): 258MB of mesh data filled the 16GB RAM and the system killed the process; the AI lowered the precision and reran, shrinking the mesh to 64MB to get it through
The dance splits into 8 sections aligned to the music beat (128 BPM), twin tails swung by 'spring' physics; the soundtrack is also synthesized in code (Am-F-C-G electro-pop), no ready-made song
3 render crashes (frame_end left unset, new filenames polluted by an old template) were all found and fixed by the AI itself, with no human help
